findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-scope AC1/AC2 to point at a durable artifact (the recorded verdict/evidence block on the ticket) or mark them satisfied-by-the-Disposition-section, so their done-state is unambiguous.

findings.finding: AC1 and AC2 are one-time investigation attestations ('recorded on this ticket') rather than durable repo end-states, and both appear already satisfied by the plan's own Disposition/Root-cause sections.
scenarios: A verifier checks AC1/AC2 and cannot tell whether they demand new work or merely restate the completed investigation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the standalone `rebar verify-completion` CLI exit-code path (_llm_commands.py:321) as a touch point for the verdict_obtainable fault routing, or state why the retryable exit is scoped to the close path only.
evidence: Plan: 'close_precheck.py:543: check verdict_obtainable BEFORE the != PASS branch and route it ... with retryable exit 11 instead of 1' — only close_precheck is named for exit routing
_cli/_llm_commands.py:321: `return 0 if result.get("verdict") == "PASS" else 1` — the standalone CLI verdict->exit consumer, unenumerated
Step 1 already names 'standalone verify-completion' as an in-scope fetch=True consumer, so this path is within the plan's scope
findings.finding: Step 2 claims 'Touch points, all of them' but omits the standalone `rebar verify-completion` CLI exit-code path, which maps verdict!=PASS to a flat exit 1 — a verdict_obtainable=false verifier fault would NOT get the retryable exit the plan promises for that class.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2 (Touch points list); consumer: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:321
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar verify-completion <id>` directly and the verifier returns a bare FAIL (verdict_obtainable=false); they receive exit 1 (permanent) instead of the intended retryable exit, defeating the fault-vs-unmet-criterion distinction outside the close path
findings.suggested_fix: Add _cli/_llm_commands.py's verify-completion exit mapping to step 2's touch-point list: route verdict_obtainable=false to the same retryable exit 11 the LLMError path already uses (_llm_error_exit_code), so a verifier fault is retryable regardless of entry point.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the fetch=True path confirms tracker HEAD is at-or-ahead of `origin/tickets` after reconverge (reconverge returns None regardless), so the confirm-or-fall-back invariant in AC4 has a concrete, testable mechanism.
evidence: Plan: 'force an UN-throttled reconverge of the tracker ... then pin tracker HEAD. If that reconverge cannot CONFIRM HEAD is at-or-ahead of `origin/tickets` (failure, lock timeout, swallowed error), fall back to today's exact behaviour'

src/rebar/_store/sync.py:199-258 — reconverge(...) -> None returns None on success AND on RebaseGuard, ConfigError, fetch failure, missing ref, and LockTimeout, with no return value or exception distinguishing at-or-ahead from fell-behind
The at-or-ahead test (`merge-base --is-ancestor remote HEAD`) exists only INSIDE _do_reconverge (sync.py:163) and is not surfaced to callers

AC4: 'a regression test proves a snapshot taken with fetch=True still contains everything origin/tickets holds (including via the confirm-or-fall-back path)' — the confirm step it tests is unspecified
findings.finding: The fetch=True reconverge branch attributes an at-or-ahead confirmation signal to rebar._store.sync.reconverge, but that function returns None on both success and every failure/early-out path and exposes no such signal — the 'confirm-or-fall-back' mechanism the plan (and AC4) rely on has no described implementation.
scenarios: reconverge silently early-returns (single-branch clone refspec miss, lock contention, rebase-in-progress) leaving tracker HEAD behind origin/tickets; the plan pins the behind-HEAD sha believing reconverge confirmed at-or-ahead, so fetch=True consumers (review-plan, standalone verify-completion, MCP) silently lose content that origin/tickets holds
The AC4 'confirm-or-fall-back path' test has no concrete branch to exercise
findings.suggested_fix: State that after the reconverge, materialize_tickets performs an explicit `git -C <tracker> merge-base --is-ancestor <remote>/tickets HEAD` (0 => at-or-ahead => pin tracker HEAD; non-zero, or the fetch/rev-parse of `<remote>/tickets` failing => fall back to resolve_ref(f'{remote}/tickets', fetch=True)); reconverge itself yields no such signal.

evidence: Plan Step 2: 'Touch points, all of them:' listing only reconcile_verdict, gate_ops.completion_reconcile, completion_sidecar, close_precheck.py:543, and completion_verdict.schema.json

findings.finding: Step 2 claims to enumerate 'Touch points, all of them' for the new `verdict_obtainable` marker set inside `reconcile_verdict`, but omits the standalone `verify-completion` CLI command `_cmd_verify_completion` (`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:321`), which reads the reconciled verdict and computes `return 0 if result.get('verdict') == 'PASS' else 1`. That path calls `reconcile_verdict` via `verify_completion`'s tail (`completion.py:513`), so it will carry `verdict_obtainable=false` but still exit 1 (bare fail), never the retryable exit 11 the plan reserves for a verifier fault.
findings.location: Implementation plan, Step 2: 'Touch points, all of them:' (reconcile_verdict/gate_ops.completion_reconcile/completion_sidecar/close_precheck.py:543/schema)
scenarios: `rebar verify-completion <id>` producing a verdict_obtainable=false result exits 1 (indistinguishable from a substantive FAIL) instead of the retryable exit 11 the plan intends for a verifier fault — the standalone CLI consumer is left unpatched.
Human/automation invoking the standalone command cannot distinguish a verifier fault from a genuine unmet-criteria FAIL, defeating Step 2's stated goal on that path.
findings.suggested_fix: In Step 2, extend the touch-point list to `_cmd_verify_completion` and have it branch on `verdict_obtainable` before the `verdict == 'PASS'` check, returning the retryable exit code (matching close_precheck's exit 11) for a verifier fault; add a regression test covering the standalone CLI exit code.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the Step-3a prompt instruction to the fresh-read regime (state the show_ticket snapshot is current-at-close) and name its placement anchor in completion_verifier.md, so a genuine absence is still reported as absent rather than uniformly softened.
evidence: Plan Step 3a: 'gains an explicit instruction that an absence observed via show_ticket must be reported as "not visible in the ticket snapshot I read", never as a claim the record does not exist' — placement in the prompt unspecified.

Plan Step 1 makes the ticket-store pin 'current-at-close by construction', so after the fix the snapshot the model reads equals the live store at close time; an absence there is authoritative, not merely 'the snapshot I read'.

The prompt is ~300 lines with no anchor named for the new instruction (verified full body of completion_verifier.md); a negation instruction ('never claim...') is a pink-elephant antipattern when not scoped to when the framework has confirmed the store is fresh.
findings.finding: Step 3a adds a negative/softening instruction to the completion_verifier prompt ('an absence observed via show_ticket must be reported as "not visible in the ticket snapshot I read", never as a claim the record does not exist') without specifying WHERE in the ~300-line prompt it lands, and the instruction is in tension with Step 1's own fix: once the pin is current-at-close, an absence in the model's show_ticket snapshot IS authoritative for the close moment, so blanket-softening every absence could undersell a genuine absence.
scenarios: A ticket record legitimately does not exist / was deleted; the model, obeying the softened wording, reports 'not visible in the snapshot I read' and the operator reads it as a possibly-stale-read caveat rather than a real absence.
The new line is placed far from the 'Untrusted input' / show_ticket sections and the model applies it inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword Step 3a so the model reports absences as 'not present in the ticket store as of the verified snapshot' (tying the phrasing to the now-current-at-close pin from Step 1) and specify it be added under the existing show_ticket / 'How to verify each requirement' section, avoiding a bare 'never say it does not exist' negation.

findings.finding: The plan bundles two independent defects with distinct root causes and code paths: (1) the stale ticket-snapshot pin (repo_snapshot.py/gate_source.py/close_precheck fetch semantics) and (2) the bare-FAIL indistinguishability channel (verdict_obtainable across completion.py/gate_ops/sidecar/schema). Each is separately reproduced (incident 1 vs incident 3), each has its own acceptance criteria, and each could ship and deliver value on its own — the snapshot fix does not depend on the verdict_obtainable channel, and vice versa.

findings.finding: For the fetch=True path, the plan's 'ensure_fresh THEN pin tracker HEAD' does not unconditionally match today's direct origin/tickets fetch-and-pin, because ensure_fresh is throttled (<=1/min) and best-effort (reconverge failures/lock-timeouts swallowed).
findings.location: Implementation plan step 1, fetch=True bullet; AC 'The fetch=True consumers ... still contains everything origin/tickets holds'
findings.suggested_fix: On the fetch=True path, either force an un-throttled reconverge before pinning (e.g. a gate-specific ensure_fresh call that ignores the <60s marker) or, when reconverge cannot confirm HEAD is at/ahead of origin/tickets, fall back to today's direct resolve_ref(f'{remote}/{ref}', fetch=True) pin — so the 'no content lost' invariant holds unconditionally, not just when the throttle window happens to be open.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the prompt path to src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md and either cite the exact line(s) that make show_ticket authoritative over the fenced context or restate Root cause 1b's mechanism in terms of what the prompt actually says (show_ticket is the read-only ticket-reading tool; the fence is untrusted data) plus where the <untrusted_ticket_context> label is generated (gate_ops.py:229).
evidence: Plan: 'The prompt labels the context <untrusted_ticket_context> and names show_ticket authoritative (reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28), so the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot.'

src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28 reads: 'You have read-only access to the repository through your file tools, and a read-only show_ticket tool to read this ticket and any related ticket ... You cannot modify, transition, sign, or close anything' — no 'authoritative' framing and no fence label.
search_files for 'authoritative' returns zero hits in src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md.
The <untrusted_ticket_context> fence is emitted by gate_ops.py:229 (f"<untrusted_ticket_context>\n{context}\n</untrusted_ticket_context>"), not by lines 26-28 of the prompt.
The actual prompt path is src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md (per index.json:22, ADR 0043, and test references), not reviewers/completion_verifier.md as cited.
findings.finding: The confident assertion in Root cause 1b that the verifier prompt 'names show_ticket authoritative (reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28)' is refuted by the actual prompt: lines 26-28 of src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md only describe show_ticket as a read-only tool, the token 'authoritative' does not appear anywhere in the file, and lines 26-28 do NOT contain the <untrusted_ticket_context> label (that fence is generated in gate_ops.py:229). The cited path is also wrong: the file is src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md, not reviewers/completion_verifier.md. This is the load-bearing premise for Root cause 1b's conclusion that 'the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot.'
scenarios: Root cause 1b's diagnosis (why the model trusted the stale snapshot over the live fenced context) rests on a prompt attribute that does not exist as described.
Step 3(a) edits 'reviewers/completion_verifier.md' at a path that does not exist, so the edit could be applied to the wrong or no file.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28' with 'src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md'; ground the 'authoritative' claim on the actual untrusted-input framing (lines 30-37) that instructs the model the ticket context is untrusted data while show_ticket is its read-only tool, and attribute the <untrusted_ticket_context> fence to gate_ops.py:229.

findings.finding: Step 2 changes reconcile_verdict's output (a new 'indeterminate/no-verdict-obtainable' outcome for non-PASS + zero findings + zero criteria), but reconcile_verdict has consumers outside completion.py that the plan does not enumerate: the workflow close-gate path gate_ops.completion_precheck (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:297) and the sidecar completion_sidecar.py:323. The close path the plan describes runs through gate_ops (which also stamps `certifiable` and feeds the signed close attestation), not directly through close_precheck's reconcile call.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; Acceptance Criteria bullet 5
findings.suggested_fix: Add gate_ops.completion_precheck (gate_ops.py:297) and completion_sidecar.py:323 to the plan's touch points; specify the indeterminate verdict's representation (e.g. verdict string value and its interaction with `certifiable`/signing and the completion_verdict schema's 'PASS or FAIL' verdict field) so every consumer maps it to the retryable-11/fail-closed contract.

findings.finding: Step 2 introduces an 'indeterminate' / 'no verdict obtainable' state for the completion_verdict LLM structured-output contract, but never defines its value vocabulary in the contract's `verdict` enum, which today admits exactly PASS/FAIL and is enforced by a normalizing validator that coerces any non-PASS value to FAIL.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; Acceptance Criteria line 'A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria is reported as "no verdict obtainable"'
findings.suggested_fix: Represent indeterminate as a distinct top-level field (e.g. `verdict_obtainable: false`) rather than a third verdict value, so the PASS/FAIL enum and its fail-safe validator stay intact; have close_precheck check that field before the `!= PASS` branch and route it to exit 11 with the distinct message.

findings.finding: Step 2 introduces an 'indeterminate' / 'no verdict obtainable' state for completion verification but never defines how it is represented in the completion_verdict structured-output contract whose verdict vocabulary is exactly {PASS, FAIL} — and three separate points coerce/validate any non-PASS token back to FAIL.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; AC line 'A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria is reported as "no verdict obtainable"'
findings.suggested_fix: State whether indeterminacy is carried as a new field (e.g. `verdict=FAIL` plus a distinct `verdict_class='indeterminate'`/`no_verdict` marker, preserving the {PASS,FAIL} enum and fail-closed blocking) or a third verdict token; if the latter, enumerate the required updates to _norm_verdict, reconcile_verdict, _schema_verdict, and the completion_verifier/finalizer prompts so the token is not coerced away. close_precheck then reads that marker to choose exit 11 vs 1.

findings.finding: Step 2 changes reconcile_verdict's output (a non-PASS/empty-findings verdict becomes 'indeterminate' rather than a synthesized '(unspecified)' finding) but enumerates only close_precheck as the affected downstream consumer. reconcile_verdict has three structural call sites; two are omitted: gate_ops.completion_reconcile (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:297) and completion_sidecar.build_payload (src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:323).
findings.location: Implementation plan, Step 2: 'In reconcile_verdict, a non-PASS verdict carrying zero findings AND zero criteria is recorded as indeterminate ... close_precheck reports it with a distinct message'

findings.finding: Step 3 instructs to change 'the verifier prompt' to stop asserting a record 'does not exist', but the completion verifier prompt contains no such wording — the misleading 'does not exist' assertion is model-generated finding text, and the framework-authored remediation string is elsewhere — so the edit site named in the plan does not exist as described.
